newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SENATOR WARNS GREENSPAN OF DEBIT CARD RISKS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SENATOR WARNS GREENSPAN OF DEBIT CARD RISKS.

text.p: U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato warned Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday about the security risk associated with the recent rapid expansion of unsolicited debit cards.

"Millions of offline debit cards are being issued by banks to their customers, almost entirely due to the mailing of unsolicited cards," D'Amato, who also chairs the Senate Banking Committee, wrote in a letter to the Fed chief.
"I am very concerned that existing regulations may not adequately inform consumers of the potential risks posed by the new cards."

The New York Republican added that consumers may be "shocked" to find out that debit cards, which resemble credit cards and often carry MasterCard or Visa logos, require no personal identification number for use and may have no liability limit if lost or stolen.
In the letter, D'Amato said approximately 25 million cards were outstanding in 1994. By 1996, the total exceeded 60 million.
